official.deadline_note: No single central deadline is published. The European Commission's Erasmus Mundus students page states: 'In most cases, you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.' Each consortium sets and publishes its own deadline on its programme website, so applicants must confirm the exact date with the specific joint master they apply to.
official.application_cycle: Applications are in most cases submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year; a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the EACEA catalogue each year
official.status_note: The official students page states that 'Students from all over the world are welcome', that 'Full scholarships are available for the best students', and that a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the catalogue each year, with applications in most cases submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Erasmus+ Programme Guide, Part B, Erasmus Mundus action: 'projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders' and 'Selected projects cannot charge student application fees.' The students page adds that scholarships 'cover your participation costs'.
benefits: Full scholarships are available for the best students; the scholarship is calculated as 1 400 Euros/month for the duration of the Master programme (12, 18 or 24 months)

The scholarship covers travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs for the entire period needed to complete the study programme, including study, research, placement, thesis preparation and defence
Scholarship holders cannot be charged tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs, and projects cannot charge student application fees
The unit contribution to institutional costs includes full insurance coverage for enrolled students
Joint degree or multiple degree certificates issued by at least two institutions of the consortium
Top-up scholarships for students from targeted world regions and special-needs support contributions (EUR 3 000 up to EUR 60 000) for students with disabilities
eligibility: Students from all over the world are welcome; EMJM scholarships can be offered to students from all over the world

Applicants must have a bachelor's degree (first degree) or be in their last year of bachelor studies, and must graduate before the master's programme starts; a bachelor's equivalent level of learning officially recognised in the degree-awarding country is also accepted
Students who have previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible to apply for an additional scholarship under the EMJM
The scholarship is awarded for full-time enrolment only and only in full for the whole programme duration (reduced duration possible with recognition of prior learning, minimum one academic year)
Consortia must ensure geographical balance: no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation may go to candidates of the same nationality
Programmes involve at least three institutions from at least three different countries, at least two of which are EU Member States or third countries associated to the Programme
requirements: Compulsory physical mobility for all enrolled students: a minimum of two study periods in two countries, at least one of which must be an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme, and both different from the student's country of residence at enrolment
Each of the two mandatory study periods must correspond to at least one academic semester (30 ECTS credits or equivalent)
A Student Agreement must be signed by the enrolled student and the EMJM consortium upon enrolment; the Student Agreement template must be published on the EMJM's website
The scholarship can only be awarded in full, to full-time students, calculated pro-rata of the actual number of days needed to complete the programme
documents: Proof of a first higher education degree (bachelor) or of an officially recognised bachelor-equivalent level of learning in the degree-awarding country

Each master's website publishes the details of the course of study, participating universities, entry requirements and all the steps of the application process (with and without scholarship); no single central document list exists
selection_criteria: Masters may offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide
Student selection, recruitment and monitoring fall under the sole responsibility of the EMJM consortium and must be organised transparently, impartially and equitably
The consortium's joint admission, selection and scholarship allocation principles are defined in the EMJM Partnership Agreement
coverage: Participation costs: scholarship holders cannot be charged tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to participation in the course; institutional unit costs also include full insurance coverage for enrolled students
application_method: Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme
Search the Erasmus Mundus course catalogue (EACEA) for the latest programmes on offer, then apply through the consortium's own website

Most master's programmes require applications between October and January for courses commencing the following academic year; applicants should visit the programme's official website and contact the consortium for information on courses, application procedures and scholarship availability
official.application_route: Choose a programme from the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue and apply directly to the consortium via the programme's own application portal (there is no central EU application form)
official.study_mode: Full-time (the scholarship can only be awarded in full and to full-time students)
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction: scholarships can be offered to students from all over the world, subject to the rule that no more than 10% of scholarships may go to candidates of the same nationality. Mobility must take place in two countries different from the student's country of residence at enrolment.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - students from all over the world are welcome; Portugal is an EU Member State, so Portuguese-linked consortia participate as Programme Country partners
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits); the scholarship is awarded for the entire duration of the Master programme, i.e. 12, 18 or 24 months
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international masters, jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries. They typically include periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence, and award either a joint degree or multiple degrees. Full scholarships are available for the best-ranked students worldwide.
official.region: Europe (study in at least two European countries, at least one of which must be an EU Member State or third country associated to the Programme)
official.program_type: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM), Erasmus+ 'Erasmus Mundus action' (Part B of the Erasmus+ Programme Guide, 2026 version of 12.11.2025); programmes are managed by consortia of higher education institutions and administered with the European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA)

not_confirmed: english_requirement - the official pages publish no central English test score; each consortium defines its own language policy and entry requirements on the programme website
deadline_central - no single central deadline exists; the official wording is that applications are in most cases submitted between October and January, with each consortium setting its own deadline
research_requirement - no central research-proposal requirement is published; programmes typically include research and thesis work as part of the curriculum
subject_or_agency_requirement - no central field or agency restriction is published; the field of study is defined by each consortium
verification.notes: The amount (1 400 EUR/month for the full programme duration) and the coverage wording (travel, visa, installation, subsistence; no tuition or application fees for scholarship holders) were taken from the Erasmus+ Programme Guide 2026 page on the Erasmus Mundus action. Programme structure, eligibility and the October-January application window come from the European Commission's Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters students page (last updated 26 June 2025). Portugal-specific evidence: the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue filtered to Portugal lists 70 EMJM projects, and Portuguese institutions such as Universidade de Lisboa, Universidade do Porto, Universidade Nova de Lisboa, Universidade de Coimbra, Universidade do Minho, Universidade Catolica Portuguesa and Instituto Politecnico do Porto appear as participating universities. The Portugal subpage URL given in the assignment (…/erasmus-mundus-joint-masters/portugal) now returns HTTP 404; the live official entry point is the main EMJM students page, which is used here as the official source and application link.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a family of EU-funded joint masters rather than one programme: you pick a course from the EACEA catalogue (70 currently listed with Portuguese partners) and apply straight to its consortium, with scholarship selection made by that consortium alone. The published award is EUR 1 400 per month for the whole 12, 18 or 24 months of study - roughly EUR 33 600 over a two-year track - and it explicitly covers travel, visa, installation and subsistence, while scholarship holders are barred from being charged tuition or application fees. Because deadlines are set per consortium and usually fall between October and January for an autumn start, the practical task is shortlisting Portugal-linked consortia early and tracking each one's own portal and document list.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong final-year bachelor or recent graduates from any country who want a multi-country European master's and can commit to full-time study in at least two different European countries
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist Portugal-linked EMJM programmes from the EACEA catalogue and open each consortium's own website to confirm the current cycle's deadline, required file and scholarship quota
Confirm you hold (or will hold before the start date) a first higher education degree or an officially recognised bachelor-equivalent qualification
Check you have never held an EMJM scholarship before, since a previous EMJM scholarship permanently blocks a new one
Prepare transcripts, degree certificate, CV, motivation letter and language evidence in the exact format the consortium portal requests
Verify you can undertake compulsory physical mobility in two countries different from your country of residence, each at least one academic semester (30 ECTS)
Contact the consortium directly with any eligibility or scholarship-availability question before the deadline, as EACEA advises
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the wrong round: each consortium sets its own October-January deadline, so missing one programme's window by days ends that route for a year
Being a final-year student whose degree will not be completed and officially awarded before the programme starts, which violates the must-graduate rule
Submitting a generic, non-consortium-specific motivation letter instead of evidencing fit with the joint programme structure and mobility track
Assuming the scholarship follows automatically from admission: only the best-ranked applicants are funded, and each programme awards a limited number of scholarships
Ignoring the 10% same-nationality rule when choosing which programmes to apply to, which shapes competition strength for your passport
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: A modest one-off personal contribution is likely for items the fixed monthly allowance does not fully absorb in high-cost cities (deposit and rent above the subsistence allowance, local transport passes, and any pre-arrival costs before the first monthly payment); programmes also include thesis, placement and inter-country moves between semesters that must be budgeted from the monthly allowance itself.
document_audit: Degree proof must be the officially recognised first-cycle qualification; if you apply while in your final bachelor year you must show the award will be granted before the programme starts
Consortia differ on certified copies, sworn translations and language of documents - follow each programme's own file specification rather than a generic checklist
The Student Agreement you must sign at enrolment is the legal basis of your scholarship terms; read the mobility, duration and recognition clauses before signing
alerts: The award is a single monthly amount (EUR 1 400), not a tuition waiver: tuition freedom for scholarship holders comes from the rule that consortia may not charge them tuition or participation fees, so confirm the programme is EU-funded in the current catalogue edition before assuming scholarship availability
Scholarships are full-time and full-duration only; part-time study or a shortened programme (recognition of prior learning, one academic year minimum) changes the award
Deadlines cluster October-January for the following academic year, overlapping with other application seasons - build a tracker rather than planning per programme
Applications go directly to each consortium, never through a central EU portal, so any site asking you to pay an application fee or promising an Erasmus Mundus place for a fee is a scam
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Shortlist from the EACEA catalogue, then apply through the chosen consortium's own online application (with-scholarship track) before its October-January deadline; the consortium ranks applicants and awards scholarships directly
